title: OpenPlayX — Your media. Your rules.
description: A local-first media player with a personal library, an AI assistant and an open MCP ecosystem. Download for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and Android TV.
intro: From the files on your Mac to the collection on your NAS. One place to watch, discover, and do a little more with AI.
previewSub: A collection that feels like yours.

aiHint: Illustrative workflow. You choose the model and services.
sourceSub: Local folders, network storage, or the media server you already use.
featuresTitle:
A player. A library.
Room to make it yours.
featuresIntro: Start with a video. Connect a collection. Add capabilities when you want them.
feature1: Turn local folders and network sources into a browsable library, with artwork, film and episode details, and a place to pick up where you left off.
feature2: A Flutter interface built around libVLC. Playback speed, audio tracks, subtitles, and familiar controls, without rebuilding your media collection.
feature3: Connect your own model API. Let the agent search media or start subtitle and media-processing tasks through the app’s tools. You stay in the loop for actions that need confirmation.
feature4: Your library and playback work without an AI account. Use on-device speech recognition, or choose an external service when you need it.

faq: Does OpenPlayX include movies or shows?
No. It is a player for your own media and services you connect. OpenPlayX does not provide a bundled film or TV catalogue.
Do I need AI to use it?
No. Playback and your local library work without a model account. Add your own model API and optional services when you want AI features.
The current release offers {platforms}. The download page lists the packages and architectures available for this version.

Original main app code is licensed under MIT. Builds linking sing-box must also comply with its GPL terms. Ecosystem services have their own MIT or GPL licenses, and some app build dependencies remain private. Check each repository and the app’s third-party notices for redistribution and corresponding-source requirements.
Can I sync everything between devices?
Cross-device library and playback sync is a design goal, not a finished feature today. Local playback, source access and the current AI tools are available independently.

A player that grows
with your ideas.
ecoPageIntro: A collection of small, focused MCP services. Self-host the capabilities you need, connect a compatible client, and keep control of your setup.
connectSteps: Follow its repository for runtime, configuration and license details.
Open AI → External capabilities. Enter the service URL and authentication.
OpenPlayX probes the MCP endpoint and lists supported tools for the agent.
ecoNotice: These are independent services, not bundled media sources. Third-party data and services have separate usage terms. MCP compatibility depends on the supported transport, authentication and schema. Live TV is outside the current scope.
contributeIntro: Good software is a collection of thoughtful contributions. Yours could be a bug report, a translation, a better interaction—or a new capability.
contributeCards: Tell us your device, version, media source, steps and expected result. A small, reproducible issue helps more than “it does not work”.
Pick a focused change. For a larger feature, discuss the scope in an issue first. Include the platform and validation you actually performed.
Create or improve an independently deployable MCP service. Keep credentials out of tools and logs, document its schema, and add useful tests.
Help with translations, accessibility, documentation and platform testing. You do not need to write a new feature to make a real difference.
contributeNote: App and service licenses are not interchangeable. Check the relevant repository before contributing or redistributing. Never put credentials, private media paths or copyrighted sample files in a public issue.
privacyTitle: A small website. A clear boundary.
privacyIntro: This website introduces OpenPlayX. It is not the player and does not connect to your media library.
privacyItems: This website uses PostHog US for usage analytics, covering page visits, referral domains and campaigns, download clicks, browser/device and screen information, approximate IP-derived location, page performance, errors, interaction heatmaps and session replay. Inputs and file-upload controls are masked or blocked; request bodies and headers are not recorded. Raw IP addresses are discarded before event storage. Anonymous browser profiles help measure repeat visits. We do not add advertising trackers, account registration or a mailing list. Cloudflare serves the site and may process connection and security information under its own policies.
Installers are hosted on GitHub Releases. Following a download or repository link takes you to GitHub and its policies apply.

Local playback is separate from AI. Models and external services may receive information you choose to use with them. The app currently stores configuration and credentials in its local configuration database; it does not promise end-to-end encryption or automatic cloud sync.

Documentation uses the same PostHog project. Each document navigation records one page view. Search terms, query strings and fragments are excluded from document analytics. Documentation search runs locally in your browser.

linuxTarDesc: Extract the archive and run ./openplayx. Requires system VLC, libsecret, GTK 3 and WebKitGTK libraries.
tvDesc: For Android TV and Google TV devices. Download the TV APK and install it on your television or streaming box.
